title: The First War of Independence (Revolt of 1857)
description: Sepoys in Meerut mutinied against British officers on May 10, 1857, marching to Delhi to proclaim Emperor Bahadur Shah Zafar as the sovereign leader of India. The uprising quickly united sepoys, royal rulers, zamindars, and peasants across northern and central India.
impact: Ended East India Company rule and brought India directly under the British Crown via the Royal Proclamation of 1858, igniting modern anti-colonial national consciousness.

title: Formation of the Indian National Congress
description: Seventy-two delegates from across India assembled at Gokuldas Tejpal Sanskrit College in Bombay to form the Indian National Congress under the leadership of W.C. Bonnerjee, Allan Octavian Hume, Dadabhai Naoroji, and Pherozeshah Mehta.
impact: Provided the first pan-Indian constitutional platform for national dialogue, civil rights petitions, and anti-imperialist political mobilization.

title: Partition of Bengal & Swadeshi Movement
description: Viceroy Lord Curzon enforced the partition of Bengal on communal lines. In response, Rabindranath Tagore, Bal Gangadhar Tilak, and Aurobindo Ghose led the Swadeshi Movement, calling for the boycott of foreign cloth and promotion of indigenous industries.
impact: Popularized the slogans 'Vande Mataram' and 'Swadeshi', sparking boycott movements and radical revolutionary organizations across Bengal and Maharashtra.

title: Home Rule Movement
description: Bal Gangadhar Tilak and Annie Besant launched twin Home Rule Leagues across India to demand self-government (Swaraj) for India within the British Empire.
impact: Tilak gave the historic declaration: 'Swaraj is my birthright and I shall have it', establishing self-rule as the central demand of India's freedom struggle.

title: Champaran Indigo Satyagraha
description: Mahatma Gandhi arrived in Bihar at the invitation of Raj Kumar Shukla to investigate the exploitation of tenant farmers forced under the oppressive Tinkathia system to grow indigo for European planters.
impact: Marked Mahatma Gandhi's first civil disobedience experiment on Indian soil, forcing the British government to abolish the compulsory indigo cultivation system.

title: Jallianwala Bagh Massacre
description: On Baisakhi day, Brigadier-General Reginald Dyer ordered British troops to open fire without warning on thousands of unarmed men, women, and children gathered at Jallianwala Bagh to protest the draconian Rowlatt Act and the arrest of Dr. Saifuddin Kitchlew and Dr. Satyapal.
impact: Over 1,000 peaceful protesters were killed. Rabindranath Tagore renounced his Knighthood in protest, and Gandhi launched the Non-Cooperation Movement.

title: Non-Cooperation Movement
description: The Indian National Congress adopted Gandhi's Non-Cooperation resolution, calling on Indians to surrender British titles, boycott government schools, law courts, and foreign cloth, and adopt Khadi and indigenous self-reliance.
impact: Unprecedented mass participation paralyzed colonial administration until its suspension following the violent Chauri Chaura incident in February 1922.

title: Kakori Train Action
description: Members of the Hindustan Republican Association (HRA) intercepted the 8-Down train at Kakori to seize British government funds intended for armed procurement.
impact: Demonstrated the strategic daring of youth revolutionaries. Ram Prasad Bismil, Ashfaqulla Khan, Roshan Singh, and Rajendra Lahiri were hanged by the British in December 1927.

title: Dandi Salt Satyagraha
description: Mahatma Gandhi and 78 chosen marchers set out on a 240-mile trek from Sabarmati Ashram to the coastal village of Dandi. On April 6, 1930, Gandhi picked up a lump of natural salt, breaking the British salt laws.
impact: Triggered countrywide civil disobedience, leading to over 60,000 arrests and focusing global press attention on India's moral struggle for independence.

title: Quit India Movement (August Kranti)
description: At the All-India Congress Committee session in Bombay, Gandhi issued the uncompromising call: 'Do or Die' (Karo ya Maro). The next morning British authorities arrested all senior Congress leaders, triggering spontaneous parallel governments across Satara, Midnapore, and Ballia.
impact: Proved to British rulers that holding India by military force was permanently unsustainable.

title: Azad Hind Government & INA Campaign
description: Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose proclaimed the Provisional Government of Azad Hind in Singapore and launched the Indian National Army (Azad Hind Fauj) with the war cry 'Chalo Dilli'.
impact: The subsequent Red Fort trials of INA officers in 1945 sparked widespread unrest and revolts across the Royal Indian Air Force and Royal Indian Navy.

title: Dawn of Independence
location: Red Fort & Constituent Assembly, New Delhi
description: At midnight on August 14-15, 1947, India shattered almost two centuries of British imperial rule. Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru delivered the historic 'Tryst with Destiny' address as the Indian Tricolor replaced the Union Jack atop the Red Fort.
impact: Born as a sovereign, democratic republic, ending colonial rule and inspiring anti-imperialist independence movements across Asia and Africa.
